text:
Only for your lips is my blood ripe,
with summer's obsession, prepared for your kisses,
always faithful to my arms and full of beauty—
my arms bloodless each night, unscathed at every dawn.

If the forests of hunting and adventure crackle
and the high birds mock us for being imprisoned,
do not let your eyes draw the bitterness
of those who have not carried love in their bones.

Stay between my arms, for you have only me,
while the others hate you, while the heart stalks you
in the warm beats of the belly
and of the temples.

See, there are no gardens beyond this wall,
which is all a long oblivion. And if my love holds you tight,
you will see an open sky behind
the dark weeping.

"Tigers in the Garden," 1968

translation.title: Siesta at the Lookout
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's intimate address, hunting and garden imagery, and the closing vision of sky behind dark weeping. Source tabs that visibly split single verse lines were folded; stanza breaks were retained.
